questions.prompt: A bacterial capsule made of repeating sugar units binds many B cell receptors on one B cell at once. What happens?

options.text: The B cell activates without helper T cells
The B cell becomes a natural killer cell
The B cell undergoes programmed cell death
The B cell must wait for a cytotoxic T cell

questions.explanation: A strong multi-receptor signal activates it on its own.

Thymus

questions.prompt: How does a T cell receptor differ from a B cell receptor?

options.text: It binds the constant region of antibodies
It is secreted in huge amounts by plasma cells
It has one binding site and is never secreted
It has five binding sites, like an IgM pentamer

questions.explanation: B cell receptors are membrane-bound antibodies (IgM).

questions.prompt: Which statement about T-dependent B cell activation is FALSE?

The helper T cell secretes interleukin to attract B cells.
The phagocyte displays antigen on MHC-2.
The B cell displays the antigen on MHC-2 for the helper T cell.

questions.explanation: Helper T cells use CD4; CD8 is on cytotoxic T cells.

questions.prompt: A liver cell infected with hepatitis virus displays viral antigens. Which display protein and which T cell are involved?

options.text: MHC-2 and a cytotoxic T cell
MHC-2 and a helper (CD4+) T cell
MHC-1 and a cytotoxic (CD8+) T cell
MHC-1 and a helper T cell

questions.explanation: Regular body cells display on MHC-1.

questions.prompt: Cytotoxic T cells kill infected cells by secreting:

options.text: Interferon and complement
IgE and IgG
Perforin and granzyme
Histamine and interleukin

questions.explanation: Perforin makes holes; granzyme triggers apoptosis.

questions.prompt: Why doesn't apoptosis cause inflammation, while necrosis does?

options.text: Necrosis is caused by T cells, which also release histamine
The dying cell calls macrophages to clean up before it spills
Apoptotic cells release extra histamine to calm the area

questions.prompt: Why don't cytotoxic T cells destroy macrophages that are displaying foreign antigens?

options.text: Cytotoxic T cells lack any T cell receptors
Macrophages never display antigens on their surface
Macrophages use MHC-2, and CD8 binds only MHC-1

questions.explanation: The CD4/CD8 system keeps immune cells safe.

questions.prompt: List the steps of T-dependent B cell activation, naming MHC-2, CD4, and interleukin.
questions.explanation: Phagocyte engulfs the pathogen and displays antigen on MHC-2 (APC) → matching helper T cell binds with TCR + CD4 → APC's interleukin activates and clones the helper T → helper T secretes interleukin to attract B cells → matching B cell binds antigen, displays it on MHC-2 → helper T binds (TCR + CD4) and secretes interleukin → B cell activated → plasma and memory cells.

questions.prompt: Compare MHC-1 and MHC-2: which cells carry each, which T cell reads each, and the outcome.
questions.explanation: MHC-1 is on all nucleated body cells and is read by cytotoxic (CD8+) T cells; a foreign antigen on MHC-1 leads to perforin/granzyme and apoptosis. MHC-2 is on antigen-presenting immune cells (macrophages, dendritic cells, B cells) and is read by helper (CD4+) T cells; it leads to activation of helper T cells and B cells.
